stem: The Gupta period is often described as the '________' of ancient India for its achievements in art, science and literature.
solution: The Gupta era is popularly called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India due to remarkable progress in many fields.

stem: The Gupta ruler celebrated in the Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) composed by Harishena was:
solution: The Prayaga Prashasti, written by his court poet Harishena, praises the conquests of Samudragupta.

stem: Because of his many military conquests, Samudragupta is sometimes called the:
solution: For his numerous conquests, Samudragupta has been nicknamed the 'Napoleon of India' by some historians.

stem: The great poet and dramatist who wrote 'Abhijnanashakuntalam' and is linked to the Gupta court was:
solution: Kalidasa, author of Shakuntala and Meghaduta, was a celebrated poet-dramatist associated with the Gupta age.

stem: The famous mathematician-astronomer of this era, who explained eclipses and worked with the concept of zero, was:
solution: Aryabhata, author of the Aryabhatiya, made pioneering contributions to astronomy and mathematics, including work related to zero and the Earth's rotation.

stem: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II was:
solution: Fa-Hien (Faxian) travelled to India during Chandragupta II's reign and left an account of Gupta society.

stem: Chandragupta II, a powerful Gupta ruler, is also known by the title:
solution: Chandragupta II bore the title 'Vikramaditya' and his reign marked a high point of Gupta power and culture.

stem: The Indian numeral system with place value and the concept of zero, refined in this period, later spread to the world through the:
solution: The decimal place-value system and zero, developed in India, were transmitted to Europe largely through Arab scholars.
